title: EventConductor cron.yaml
description: Scheduled workflow starts, in a file named cron.yaml (or cron.yml) next to the workflow definitions. Either a list of schedules, or an object whose only key is schedules holding that list. Each occurrence of each schedule creates a process instance of the named workflow with the given variables, while that workflow is ACTIVE.

id.description: Optional name of the schedule (letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'), unique across the engine. A pause is kept under it, and a schedule created from the admin UI, REST API or MCP with the same id is replaced by this entry when the file is imported: the file owns it from then on. Absent means the engine derives an id from the workflow and the entry's content.

cron.description: Spring cron expression (six fields, seconds first, e.g. "0 0 9 * * MON-FRI").

workflow.description: The id of the workflow definition each occurrence starts. An entry naming an unknown workflow is reported and skipped.

zone.description: IANA time zone the expression is read in (e.g. Europe/Madrid). Absent means the engine's workflow.time.zone (the JVM's zone unless configured).

variables.description: Initial process variables for each start, by name. Values are strings (numbers and booleans are read as their text).
